item.title: China's Bet on Physical AI
item.dc:creator: Morgan Stanley
item.description: Morgan Stanley · Thoughts on the Market — Live from Morgan Stanley's Asia Pacific Summit in Singapore, our China Equity Strategist Laura Wang joins Chief China Economist Robin Xing to explore how physical AI could rewire China's factories and what it takes for that investment to translate into stronger profits and higher incomes. Read more insights from Morgan Stanley. ----- Transcript ----- Laura Wang: Welcome to Thoughts on the Market. I'm Laura Wang, chief China Equity Strategist at Morgan Stanley Research. And on this very special episode of the podcast, we're coming to you directly from Morgan Stanley's Asia Pacific Summit in Singapore to discuss the physical AI revolution, how China is bringing AI to the real world. I'm joined by Robin Xing, Chief China Economist. Let's get started. So AI's next chapter is not just about what it says to us. It's about what it can do in the physical world, from vehicles on our roads to robots on factory floors. Our emerging frontiers research points roughly at 12 trillion US dollars of incremental industry 5.0 investment over the next 10 years. item.title: 279: How AI and Interest Rates Are Changing Corporate Credit Markets
item.dc:creator: BlackRock
item.description: BlackRock · The Bid — Corporate credit markets are facing new questions as artificial intelligence reshapes the economy and companies navigate higher borrowing costs. Billions of dollars are being invested in AI infrastructure, from data centers and semiconductors to energy and computing power. But while this investment creates opportunities for some businesses, AI disruption could threaten others, raising important questions about their ability to repay debt. In this episode of The Bid, host Oscar Pulido explores how AI investing, interest rates and changing business models are affecting corporate bonds and credit risk. Featuring insights from José Aguilar, BlackRock's Head of European Credit, alongside Tony Kim, Head of the Global Technology Team within BlackRock Fundamental Equities, Alex Brazier, BlackRock's Global Head of Investment and Portfolio Solutions, and Jean Boivin, the episode examines why understanding the financial strength of individual companies matters in an evolving market. The episode also explores how AI disruption is creating differences within the software industry. It stands as one of the most consequential events in modern market history, reshaping economies and investment thinking worldwide. This conversation traces the roots of the crisis-from the housing bubble and lax lending standards to the complex web of derivatives and leverage that amplified risk across the financial system. item.title: AI isn’t just shaping biotech narratives, it’s shifting the market
item.dc:creator: RBC Capital Markets
item.description: RBC Capital Markets · Strategic Alternatives — Artificial intelligence has long been viewed as a driver of biotech innovation, helping researchers accelerate discovery and improve productivity. But new research suggests its influence may extend beyond the lab and into market performance itself. In this episode, Rishi Jaluria, Managing Director, Software Equity Research, RBC Capital Markets, and Leonid Timashev, Biotech Analyst, RBC Capital Markets, discuss how AI-driven capital flows, adoption trends, and market risks are increasingly influencing biotech performance and investor decision-making. They explore the emerging relationship between AI and biotech, the impact of capital rotation across sectors, where AI can create value in biotech development, and the signals investors should be watching next. Key Points The relationship between AI and biotech has recently shifted from a historically positive correlation to a more inverse one, with capital flows emerging as a potential driver of biotech performance Capital rotating out of AI and semiconductors may increasingly support biotech, particularly during periods of market uncertainty and heightened volatility.
